title: FY27 Intern - ML Compiler Research Intern - 6 months, Strasbourg, France
description: Company: Qualcomm France S.A.R.L. Job Area: Interns Group, Interns Group > Interim Intern General Summary: Opportunity Overview: Join our Compiler Labs team in Strasbourg, France, for an internship focused on compiler and runtime techniques for efficient Generative AI inference on modern AI accelerators. Generative AI models increasingly require sophisticated optimization to achieve high performance within the compute, memory, and power constraints of edge devices. Traditional ML compilation approaches typically decompose a model into individual operators and optimize or schedule them separately. An alternative approach is to optimize larger portions of the model jointly, enabling more coordinated decisions about computation, data movement, memory usage, and hardware resources. During this internship, you will investigate compiler and performance-optimization techniques for these larger-scale, highly optimized execution models. Depending on your background and the direction of the project, the work may involve automatic exploration of optimization strategies, compiler-driven code generation, intermediate representations, memory planning, or performance analysis. Representative Projects: Explore automatic optimization and auto-tuning techniques for high-performance AI kernels. Investigate compiler techniques for generating and optimizing specialized implementations from model or intermediate representations. Develop profiling-guided approaches for evaluating and selecting alternative implementation strategies. Explore efficient management and reuse of on-chip memory using compiler analysis of tensor lifetimes and data dependencies. Analyze the interaction between computation scheduling, data movement, memory usage, and model structure. Evaluate new optimization techniques on representative Generative AI workloads and accelerator architectures. Develop experimental compiler or performance-analysis infrastructure to guide future optimization work. The exact research direction will be selected according to the candidate's background and interests, together with the technical opportunities available at the beginning of the internship. Toolchain & Environment The internship may involve technologies such as: C++ and Python LLVM and MLIR PyTorch and related model representations AI accelerator programming and toolchains Performance profiling and benchmarking tools Compiler optimization and code-generation infrastructure Candidate Profile We are looking for a student in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field with a strong interest in some combination of: Compilers and program optimization Machine learning systems High-performance computing Parallel programming Computer architecture Generative AI and Large Language Model inference Experience with C++, Python, LLVM/MLIR, GPU or accelerator programming, or ML frameworks is valuable, but experience in all of these areas is not required. The ideal candidate is curious, comfortable investigating open-ended technical problems, and interested in understanding the interaction between machine-learning workloads, compiler transformations, memory systems, and hardware execution. What You Will Gain Hands-on experience with compiler and performance-engineering problems for modern Generative AI workloads. Exposure to intermediate representations, code generation, accelerator execution, and quantitative performance analysis. The opportunity to build and evaluate a focused research prototype within an experienced compiler team. Experience translating experimental results into practical engineering recommendations. *References to a particular number of years experience are for indicative purposes only. title: Mainframe System Verification Tester Apprentice-2nd Shift
description: At IBM Infrastructure & Technology, we design and operate the systems that keep the world running. From high-resiliency mainframes and hybrid cloud platforms to networking, automation, and site reliability. Our teams ensure the performance, security, and scalability that clients and industries depend on every day. Working in Infrastructure & Technology means tackling complex challenges with curiosity and collaboration. You'll work with diverse technologies and colleagues worldwide to deliver resilient, future-ready solutions that power innovation. With continuous learning, career growth, and a supportive culture, IBM provides the opportunities to build expertise and shape the infrastructure that drives progress. As a Mainframe System Verification Tester Apprentice at IBM, you will work in IBM Z Engineering System Test and continue the IBM tradition of delivering world-class Z mainframes that are best of breed in Reliability, Availability, and Serviceability. Engineering Systems Test is the final stage of IBM Z server product development where the design, architecture, and code is validated and qualified. You will have the opportunity to apply your knowledge and experience using the latest tools and technologies to support IBM processors, storage or other semiconductor hardware. Throughout your apprenticeship, you will work closely with experienced engineers, technicians and other mentors in a laboratory or test floor environment to create and execute test or physical characterization plans that assess the electrical performance and characteristics against design and functional requirements. Where applicable, you will be taught principles of system analysis, defect identification and repair and/or the basics of a variety of lab safety procedures relevant to the physical preparation of samples for chemical, optical, or electrical characterization. Every graduate of a Registered Apprenticeship program receives a nationally-recognized credential from the DOL. You'll go through your first few weeks together, learning about IBM and the skills you'll be attaining throughout your apprenticeship. Then, you'll work with your managers and mentors to progress through your personal skills roadmap, learning and demonstrating new knowledge and competencies through hands-on application with your project teams.
